summary: Amrita Saikia is a Tibetology scholar who completed a PhD at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (2018–2022). She held posts at TISS, Woxsen University as assistant professor (2022), and the German Institute for Global and Area Studies (2023–2024).

Amrith Krishna is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at IIT Kharagpur, the University of Cambridge, IT University of Copenhagen, Oriflow, Uniphore (attested 2023), and Learno.AI (attested 2024–2025).
Amruta Barbadikar is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. in 2020 at the University of Hyderabad, where she also held an academic post.

Amy Heller is a Tibetologist and historian. She earned a Ph.D. at EPHE under Ariane Macdonald. Her posts include visiting roles at Yale, Sapienza, and Sichuan universities, as well as appointments at CNRS, SOAS, INALCO, and the University of Bern.

Amy L. Allocco is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She earned degrees from Colgate University, Harvard University, and Emory University (PhD, 2001–2009). She held a post at Elon University (attested 2015).

Amy Paris Langenberg is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University (~2001–2008) and served as assistant professor of religious studies at Eckerd College (~2014).

Amy Sims Miller specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her BA from Wesleyan University and her MA and PhD from the University of Virginia (2004) under David Germano, alongside studies under several traditional Tibetan teachers.

Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar of linguistics and Japanology. She earned degrees from the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1990 and 1993, and has served as a professor at the University of Washington since approximately 1995.
Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Tübingen and earned her PhD from the University of Salamanca (1965–1978), where she was appointed professor in 1979.

Anagarika Dharmapala was a Buddhist studies and religious figure. Educated at schools in Sri Lanka, including Royal College, Colombo (~1878–1883), he founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891 and the Maha Bodhi Society of India.

Anagarika Govinda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Freiburg, Naples, Cagliari, and under Tomo Geshe Rinpoche. He founded Arya Maitreya Mandala and taught at Visva-Bharati, Patna, Allahabad, Lucknow, and Banaras Hindu University.
Anagarika Munindra was a religious studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966) and Satya Narayan Goenka. He served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple from 1953 to 1957.

Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teacher Tsurlo Rinpoche and served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Anand A. Yang is a historian and Indologist. He was educated at Swarthmore College and the University of Virginia. He held posts at the University of Utah, Sweet Briar College, and the University of Washington (~2002).

Anand Venkatkrishnan works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University in 2015 and serves as Assistant Professor of the History of Religion in South Asia at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Ananda Guruge was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London. He held posts at NIEPA, California State University, Fullerton, and the University of the West.

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy was an Indologist, art historian, and philosopher. He studied at UCL and the University of London. He directed Ceylon's Mineral Survey and later served as keeper and research fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was an Indologist and historian. He served as professor and department head at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949), university professor at Patna University (~1949–1957), and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1955).

Anantalal Thakur was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Calcutta under several mentors. He served as a professor at the Mithila Institute and was director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, later serving as Emeritus Professor at St. Olaf College.
